Cc: legal@ergohealth.com

Subject: Request: artifact suppression lifecycle (prompts, outputs, service logs)

Jordan —

Thanks again for the walkthrough last week. We need to formalize our request so our compliance team can close the ticket: ErgoHealth requests permanent suppression (retirement) of all prompt/input/response artifacts and correlated service logs generated by our tenant  ergo-prod-42 across the last 36 months. In-scope items: conversational prompts, assistant outputs, KV cache derivatives, request/response traces, and any logs that contain PII identifiers. Out-of-scope: aggregated telemetry and system-level infra metrics.

Please confirm the procedural steps you will run, the expected timeline (including backups/replication windows), and what evidence you will provide so we can sign-off. We will need an attestation we can attach to our audit.

Thanks,
Alyssa Gomez
Sr. Compliance Manager | ErgoHealth
[Attachment: ergo_suppression_request_v2.pdf (PDF, 48KB)]

From: Jordan Blake <jordan.blake@redwood.ai>

Cc: Soojin Lee <soojin.lee@redwood.ai>, Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.ai>
Date: 2026-11-12T10:02:00-08:00
Subject: Re: Request: artifact suppression lifecycle (prompts, outputs, service logs)

Alyssa —

Appreciate the clear scope. High-level plan we propose: 1) open a suppression run ticket in our ops queue and snapshot the current index state; 2) identify and mark all objects linked to tenant ergo-prod-42 across S3 buckets, KV stores, and trace databases; 3) execute deletion passes in the following order to preserve evidence: prompts/outputs -> derivative KV artifacts -> request traces/logs -> archival backups; 4) run verification pass that computes SHA256 digests of deleted object manifests and produce an attestation bundle; 5) deliver evidence bundle and DocuSign attestation for ErgoHealth signature.

Timeline: we can begin the pre-checks tomorrow (Nov 13), and execute the first deletion pass on Nov 14–15, with final evidence delivered by EOD Nov 15, assuming no complications. If the window intersects any retention holds, we'll surface immediately.

I'm looping in Soojin (security ops) and Marissa (customer ops) to confirm runbook details and who will sign the attestation.

Jordan
Jordan Blake
Account Executive, Redwood Inference
[Attachment: proposed-suppression-phases.txt (plain text, 4KB)]

Jordan / Marissa —

Quick operational notes from security ops: 1) We will run a dry-run scope query to enumerate object counts and estimate runtime. That will produce an "ergo_suppression_manifest_v1.pdf" with object counts and the S3 key prefixes. 2) For request traces and service logs, we have to consider retention snapshots on our backup tier; we'll schedule deletion of snapshots after primary deletions complete (this reduces risk of accidental restore). 3) KV cache derivatives require a soft-delete marker + compaction pass; compaction runs are CPU-bound so we will throttle to maintain latency SLOs. 4) We plan two independent verifiers: a technical verifier that generates deletion manifests and SHA256 hashes, and a legal attestation template for signature.

I'll prepare the operational runbook (retirement-runbook-20261115.txt) and a CSV of verification hashes. I'll also flag any entries that intersect ongoing investigations or legal holds. If legal@ergohealth.com confirms no holds, we proceed on schedule.

Soojin

Alyssa —

Following Soojin's notes, we ran the enumeration yesterday and attached the suppression manifest that lists estimated object counts and a projected execution window. Key clarifications for your sign-off: 1) Once we delete primary objects (prompts/outputs), any derived embeddings or KV snapshots referencing those identifiers will be flagged for compaction and removal — this can take an additional 24 hours depending on size. 2) Backups: we will mark and then delete backup snapshots after primary deletion; that will cause a permanent irrecoverable state and cannot be rehydrated. 3) Evidence package will include: suppression manifest, deletion runbook, CSV of deleted object hashes (evidence-hash-list.csv) and a short executive attestation PDF which you can sign in DocuSign.

Action requested from ErgoHealth: please confirm by replying that there are no retention/legal holds and that you authorize Redwood to proceed with the suppression lifecycle as scoped. Once we receive confirmation, we'll schedule the first deletion pass for Nov 14 and deliver evidence by Nov 15.

Attachments: ergo_suppression_manifest_v1.pdf, retirement-runbook-20261115.txt, evidence-hash-list.csv

Regards,
Marissa Cole
